slides.title: A Deployable Architecture for Robot-Mediated Tasks (DART): Evaluation in Socially Assistive Robot-Guided Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Exercises
slides.highlight: DART extends socially assistive robots via cloud infrastructure to support complex tasks like cognitive behavioral therapy, aligning with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: DART extends low-cost socially assistive robots using a web application and cloud infrastructure for complex tasks.
card.key_idea: A robot-agnostic architecture distributing interaction orchestration to a web app and data/computation to the cloud, while the robot handles physical embodiment and local motor control.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via participatory design, a 103-participant in-lab study (showing reduced stress/anxiety), and a six-week in-home deployment with four participants using the Blossom robot.
card.limitation: Participants identified speech input, visual presentation, and web-robot synchronization as priority areas for improvement.

slides.title: ECHO: A Matched-Contrast Benchmark for Context-Sensitive Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Dialogue
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark to evaluate whether full-duplex systems can distinguish between interruptions and backchannels based on dialogue context. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: ECHO is a diagnostic benchmark for Chinese full-duplex dialogue to evaluate context-sensitive turn-taking decisions.
card.key_idea: It uses matched-contrast pairs where the same insertion text is paired with different dialogue contexts to distinguish between Yield (interruption) and Keep (backchannel/off-talk) actions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated four speech systems and Gemini (text reference) using Pairwise Action Success Rate (PASR). Most speech systems showed a strong bias toward yielding.
card.limitation: Uses synthesized audio rather than natural speech and lacks strict acoustic control for waveform-identical insertions across rewritten contexts.

slides.title: Audio-Visual Turn-taking Prediction in Cocktail Party Scenarios
slides.highlight: This research evaluates audio-visual predictive turn-taking models in noisy cocktail-party scenarios, providing insights into modality-specific degradation and adaptation. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling in complex environments.

card.one_liner: Audio-visual turn-taking models trained on clean data degrade significantly in noisy cocktail-party scenarios.
card.key_idea: Evaluates Voice Activity Projection (VAP) variants (Audio, Video, Multimodal) using Candor for pre-training and AVCocktail for testing, focusing on domain adaptation via fine-tuning.
card.evaluation: Tested on Candor and AVCocktail datasets using weighted F1 scores; results show multimodal models are most robust, especially after fine-tuning.
card.limitation: Fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting of the original domain, and current fusion mechanisms poorly exploit audio-visual complementarity in noise.

slides.title: Exploring Multimodal Turn-Taking Cues in Face-to-Face Conversation using Voice Activity Projection
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that integrating visual features like facial action units, gaze, and body pose improves turn-taking prediction over audio-only models, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: Visual cues from face-to-face conversations significantly improve turn-taking prediction over audio-only transformer-based models.
card.key_idea: Extends Voice Activity Projection (VAP) by fusing audio with gaze, head, body, and facial action units (FAU) using cross-attention, delta features, and trainable gating.
card.evaluation: Tested on 400 hours of Meta Seamless Interaction dataset using VAP loss and balanced accuracy for hold/shift, short/long, and pre-shift tasks.
card.limitation: Results may be upper-bounded as test splits are not dyad-disjoint, and gaze estimates are unreliable during eye occlusion.

slides.title: Rethinking the Implications of Human Feedback for Preference Learning in Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.tldr: IMPROVING ROBOT PREFERENCE LEARNING VIA DYNAMIC IMPLICATION MODELING
slides.highlight: The proposed IMPLIED method improves robot behavior adaptation during collaboration by learning to infer human preference implications more accurately than fixed rules. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: IMPLIED improves robot preference learning by dynamically revising labels for unchosen actions using human feedback.
card.key_idea: A mixture model combining a fixed-rule prior with a Gaussian Process classifier that learns to infer and revise accepted/rejected labels for unchosen actions over time.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation (sandwich-making, block-sorting) and physical pizza-making studies against fixed-rule and LLM baselines using L2 error, conflict proportion, and F1 scores.

slides.title: MP-Bench: Evaluating Voice Agents as a Multiparty Conversation Participant
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR MULTIPARTY VOICE AGENT EVALUATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces MP-Bench to evaluate voice agents' turn-taking awareness and response appropriateness in multi-party contexts, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: MP-Bench evaluates voice agents' ability to participate in multiparty conversations via turn-taking and comprehension tasks.
card.key_idea: A benchmark using synthetic audio scenarios (Discussion and Turn-based Game) to test turn-taking awareness (explicit, implicit, negative) and response appropriateness in four-participant interactions.
card.evaluation: 12 voice agents were tested; results showed realtime agents perform near chance on implicit turn-taking and below 33% on multiparty comprehension.
card.limitation: Uses synthetic audio without overlapping speech, background noise, or multi-turn engagement, creating a domain gap from real-world conversations.

slides.title: Neuro-Symbolic Hierarchical Intention Anticipation in Human Behavior
slides.highlight: This work proposes a neuro-symbolic framework for anticipating human goals across four ontological levels, supporting MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A neuro-symbolic framework for anticipating human goals across four ontological levels using hierarchical planning.
card.key_idea: A Hierarchical Planning Decoder attached to a frozen encoder, using soft neuro-symbolic regularization and hard reachability masks to ensure ontological validity and hierarchical continuity.
card.evaluation: Tested on 15,002 multimodal episodes (NTU RGB+D 120); outperformed sequential baselines in top-5 accuracy and joint logic constraint satisfaction.
card.limitation: Challenges remain in compositional goal generalization and unordered set prediction.
